messages:
ara: heads up — on-prem canary nodes started hanging after NCCL 3.5.2 bump. multiple multi-GPU inference jobs hit collective timeouts.
deploy-bot: rollout started 2277004300 (nccl:3.5.2)
sam: can you paste the error logs?
ara: here are the kernel + runtime snippets i grabbed: 
```
[1234.567890] nv_peer_mem: probe of 0000:65:00.0 failed with error -16
[1234.567891] nccl: Allreduce timed out after 120s - rank 0 -> hung
[1234.568000] nvidia_uvm: loaded, PID 4321
```
marta: seeing module pinned by process kworker/3 (kernel worker). lsof shows /dev/nvpeer0 open by containerd-shim.
lina: that's the on-prem GPU hostd -> kubelet didn't drain because PV detach stuck.
devon: any chance to force unbind the device?
marta: tried `rmmod -f nv_peer_mem` — kernel returns "device or resource busy". even `modprobe -r` fails.
sam: looks like containers still have open fd to nvpeer. which pods?
ara: inference-pool-3 had three pods pinned; one uses the low-latency model with direct NVPeer access.
ryan: i'm pulling trace logs and will check p2p links.
lina: for immediate mitigation, can we fallback those pods to the cpu/quantized variant? that would free nv_peer devices.
ara: starting fallback routing for impacted job ids now. expect ~20% throughput drop for those requests.
deploy-bot: rollback flag requested by ara.
sam: i'm preparing rollback to nccl 3.4.8 on canary hosts. note: this will require driver module dance and brief service restarts.
ara: filing infra incident INC-2026-0042. devbot: incident INC-2026-0042 created by ara.
marta: rollback playbook (short):
1) cordon node(s)
2) drain pods (allow eviction + wait for PV detach)
3) stop inference svc on node
4) apt/dep downgrade nccl -> 3.4.8
5) reload nvidia modules + verify /proc bindings

Commands we used:
```
sudo systemctl stop inference.service
sudo apt-get install -y nccl=3.4.8-1
sudo modprobe -r nv_peer_mem || true
sudo modprobe nvidia_uvm
sudo systemctl start inference.service
```

sam: watch /proc/driver/nvidia/gpus/*/information for link state and memory leaks. also monitor dmesg for nvlink train errors.
lina: can we add a pre-stop hook to daemonset to close nvpeer fds so rmmod succeeds?
marta: i'm prototyping a small daemon that sends SIGTERM to helper processes holding the device before drain. will push to canary.
ryan: on the hardware side i see one node with repeated "NVLINK link training failed" — scheduling hardware swap with on-prem ops.
ara: rollback started on 4 canary nodes in us-west1. hold global rollout.
sam: also adding a temporary policy to route multi-gpu jobs to dedicated pooled capacity (dedicated nodes) to reduce impact on shared on-prem. cost will spike; finance heads notified.
lina: creating a postmortem checklist so we add kernel guard and pre-drain hook before future nccl bumps.
driver-bot: dispatching oncall_driver -> ryan.
ryan: joining now, pulling traces and will coordinate hw swap.
ara: update: rollback finished on 3/4 nodes; one node still in "device busy" state, scheduled for manual intervention tomorrow.
marta: monitoring — no new hangs after rollback on the succeeded nodes.
sam: +1, holding global rollout and adding canary checks for pinned fd detection before future nccl upgrades.
ara: thanks all, will keep INC-2026-0042 updated. :thumbsup:
